A step function f is a function that can be written as a finite linear combination of indicator functions of intervals. In other words, f(x) = ∑_{i=1}^n c_i \mathbb{I}_{[a_i, b_i]}(x), where a_i, b_i are points in [a, b] and c_i are constants.

To prove that f is Riemann Integrable, we need to show that the upper and lower Riemann sums converge to the same value as the partition size approaches 0.

Let P be a partition of [a, b] into n subintervals, each of length Δx_i = b_i - a_i. Let F_i be the supremum of f on [a_i, b_i] and E_i be the infimum of f on [a_i, b_i]. Then, the upper Riemann sum is:

U(P) = ∑_{i=1}^n F_i \Delta x_i

and the lower Riemann sum is:

L(P) = ∑_{i=1}^n E_i \Delta x_i

Since f is a step function, we know that F_i = c_i and E_i = c_i for each i. Therefore, we have:

U(P) = ∑_{i=1}^n c_i \Delta x_i
L(P) = ∑_{i=1}^n c_i \Delta x_i

Since the summands are the same, we have:

U(P) = L(P)

This means that the upper and lower Riemann sums are equal for any partition P. Therefore, the upper and lower Riemann sums converge to the same value as the partition size approaches 0, and we have:

∫_a^b f(x) dx = lim_{Δx → 0} U(P) = lim_{Δx → 0} L(P) = ∫_a^b f(x) dx

Therefore, we have proven that a step function f / [a, b] -> \mathbb{R} is Riemann Integrable.

Note that this proof only works for step functions, which are a special type of function. In general, not all functions are Riemann Integrable.
